haiku-low.q1: The scheduler at 02:00 UTC, with retries. It extracts orders rows from the read replica with updated_at after window_lo and at most window_hi.
haiku-low.q2: The document does not say why. It states visibility can lag updated_at by up to 90 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: Edits bump updated_at, so the next night whose window covers it extracts and merges it, replacing the stored row if newer.
haiku-low.q4: It is loaded as a normal write: updated_at is bumped, and the row stays with is_deleted = true. Nothing is removed.
haiku-low.q5: Roll back, drop staging, mark row failed with error text, exit non-zero; hwm unchanged. Scheduled retries after 15 minutes, paging on-call at three failed rows.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous committed night, since they read only committed rows. A staleness alert goes to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares the last 30 creation days' counts and checksums and reloads any mismatched day.
haiku-low.q8: The merge replaces a stored row only when the staged updated_at is equal to or later than the stored one.
haiku-low.q9: In ctl.pipeline_state as hwm_ts. It is set to window_hi, only if lower, inside the commit transaction.
haiku-low.q10: One warehouse transaction covers the merge, hwm move and committed mark, so dashboards see either the old or new whole night.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is dropped by the failure handler, or by the next preflight if the attempt died. The retry extracts the same stored window.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads the day's replica rows with updated_at at most window_hi, then stages, checks and merges them. It does not move hwm_ts.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC (run_date = UTC date). It extracts orders rows with updated_at after window_lo (hwm_ts minus 2 hours) and at most window_hi (02:00 UTC of run_date), from the read replica.
sonnet.q2: The document says rows can become visible up to 90 minutes after their updated_at (hence the 2-hour lookback). It does not mention bulk imports or the cause.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so a later night's window (or the lookback overlap) extracts it. Merge replaces the stored row if staged updated_at is equal to or later than the stored one.
sonnet.q4: Deletion is a normal write that bumps updated_at. It loads like any change and the row stays in fact_orders with is_deleted = true (deleted_at set). Nothing is removed.
sonnet.q5: The failure handler rolls back, drops staging, marks the row failed with error text, and exits non-zero. hwm_ts does not change. A scheduled attempt is retried 15 minutes later with the same window. After three non-committed rows, on-call is paged and it exits 0. A manual attempt exits non-zero with no retry and no page.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous night's data (committed rows only). At 06:00 UTC a check finds no committed row for run_date and sends a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
sonnet.q7: Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation day for the last 30 days (up to window_hi), and reloads any differing day from the replica into the warehouse. This only happens if that Sunday's night commits and reconciliation finishes within the 45-minute limit.
sonnet.q8: The merge inserts new orders, and replaces an existing one only when the staged updated_at is equal to or later than the stored updated_at, so a row never moves back to an older version. Staging also must have no repeated order_id.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table ctl.pipeline_state, as hwm_ts. It is set to window_hi, only if hwm_ts is lower. This happens inside the single commit transaction, together with the merge and marking the row committed.
sonnet.q10: The commit is one warehouse transaction that does the merge, the hwm_ts move and the committed mark together. Failure before COMMIT rolls all three back. Dashboards read only committed rows from mart.fact_orders and refresh at 06:00 UTC.
sonnet.q11: The failed attempt's staging is dropped (by the failure handler, or by the next preflight if the attempt died). The retry recreates staging empty. It extracts the same stored window (window_lo and window_hi copied from the night's latest row).
sonnet.q12: It re-reads the replica rows for creation day D with updated_at at most window_hi. They go through the same stage, check and merge steps as the nightly load. It does not change hwm_ts and writes no ctl.pipeline_runs row. The result goes to ctl.recon_results.
